name: NOVONIX Limited
headquarters: Brisbane, Queensland, Australia (registered); operating base 1029 West 19th Street, Chattanooga, Tennessee, USA
employees: 192 at 31 December 2025 (126 United States, 66 Canada); the 66 Canadian roles left with the Battery Technology Solutions divestiture on 30 April 2026 and no updated total has been published
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** NOVONIX is a pre-revenue synthetic graphite anode developer whose entire investment case now rests on qualifying one plant for one lead customer, and whose auditor has flagged a material uncertainty over its ability to continue as a going concern. Continuing-operations revenue for the half year to 30 June 2026 was **zero**; the date for Riverside to reach full production capacity has moved from December 2027 to **September 2031**; and a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price cure deadline falls on **Monday 14 September 2026**, five days after this dossier was written, with the outcome unresolved.

**BACKGROUND.** An Australian company, dual-listed as ASX: NVX (ordinary shares) and Nasdaq: NVX (American depositary shares), with its operating centre in Chattanooga, Tennessee. It files a Form 20-F as a foreign private issuer and furnishes every ASX announcement as a Form 6-K. Following the sale of the Battery Technology Solutions division on 30 April 2026 it is a single-business company: synthetic graphite anode active material, made in a continuous induction furnace process it developed with Harper International, aimed at the North American battery supply chain. Auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers, Brisbane. ABN 54 157 690 830.
ecosystemRole:
NOVONIX would sit one layer above the cell makers in this corpus if it were shipping — it makes the anode active material that goes into the negative electrode of a lithium-ion cell, in the same upstream position that a lithium producer occupies on the cathode side. Graphite is chemistry-agnostic in a way cathode material is not: an LFP cell built for grid storage and a nickel-rich cell built for a vehicle both use a graphite anode, so an anode supplier is exposed to total lithium-ion demand rather than to a chemistry bet.

What makes the company interesting to a storage and datacentre corpus is not scale but structure. It claims to be "the only qualified U.S.-based supplier of battery-grade synthetic graphite anode material", in a market where China and Chinese-controlled companies are forecast to hold about 99.1% of global anode capacity in 2026 and North America is forecast to move from near zero to roughly 4% by 2035 (both figures Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, cited by the company). It is a policy-created business: a US$100m Department of Energy grant, a US$103m Section 48C investment tax credit and a conditional Department of Energy loan commitment of up to US$754.8m are what stand between the plant and the capital markets.

Its commercial commitments, however, are electric-vehicle-first. Both live offtakes — Panasonic Energy and PowerCo SE, Volkswagen's cell arm — are for vehicle cells. The company names energy storage among its target segments and cites storage-installation growth as a demand driver, but no storage-specific offtake is disclosed. The honest description is an upstream materials supplier with stated but uncontracted exposure to grid storage.

productsAndServices.name: Synthetic graphite anode active material — the Riverside plant
productsAndServices.description: The whole of the continuing business. Battery-grade synthetic graphite anode active material (AAM) made at the Riverside facility in Chattanooga, Tennessee, acquired in July 2021 for US$42.6m. The only publicly named grade is GX-23. Nameplate is 20,000 tonnes per annum; four graphitisation furnaces are fully installed and in calibration and raw-material testing. Revenue from this business to date is US$0 — the plant has produced industrial-grade material and customer samples, not commercial battery-grade sales.
highlights: First mass-production, commercial-grade industrial sample shipped in late September 2025 to what the company describes as "one of North America's largest value-added carbon processors", unnamed

First known North-American-produced synthetic graphite AAM C-sample delivered to Panasonic Energy on 11 June 2026; internal testing indicates it meets Panasonic's specifications, subject to formal validation
Battery-grade mass production targeted for the second half of 2027, moved from 2026 on 16 January 2026 and reaffirmed since

A Minviro life-cycle assessment of GX-23 found roughly 60% lower global warming potential than conventional anode-grade synthetic graphite from Inner Mongolia and roughly 30% lower than natural graphite from Heilongjiang Province
Over 100 samples went to 15 customers and prospects during 2025; the FY2025 20-F states 13 prospective customers were receiving samples
Contractual agreements to supply up to 157,000 tonnes of anode material from 2027 to 2034, per the company's own impairment-model disclosure
productsAndServices.positioning: The company's claim is categorical: "To our knowledge, we are the only qualified U.S.-based supplier of battery-grade synthetic graphite anode material." It names no competitor anywhere in its first-party materials, framing competition in four categories instead — Asian synthetic producers, natural graphite miners, other graphitisation companies and US entrants, and disruptive chemistries such as silicon anodes. Independent data puts that claim in proportion: SNE Research counted 2.11 million tonnes of global anode shipments in 2024, of which artificial graphite was 1.76 Mt or 83.2%, and all ten of the largest producers are Chinese — BTR at 432 kt-plus and Shanshan at 340 kt, with POSCO Future M falling to eleventh. A 20,000 tpa plant is under 1% of that market and about 4.6% of BTR's single-company volume. Against Western peers, Syrah Resources' Vidalia is further along at 11,250 tpa with production since early 2024. The defensible typing is aspirant rather than incumbent or challenger — there is no shipped commercial volume to contest anyone with.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, under binding offtake agreements conditioned on qualification milestones, with an agreed market-based price formula in each case. No contract price is public; the company's own impairment model assumes a realised US$7–11/kg, cut from US$10–12/kg a year earlier, against operating costs of US$6–8/kg.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Electric-vehicle cells, stationary energy storage, defence, drones, aerospace, telecommunications, medical devices, consumer electronics, and industrial non-battery graphite
productsAndServices.roadmap: Full production capacity at Riverside is now targeted for September 2031, extended from December 2027 — the company's stated reason is "management's conscious decision to conserve capital and reduce near-term spending". A second site, NOVONIX Enterprise South, is a 182-acre parcel in the Enterprise South Industrial Park with an initial 31,500 tpa design and 450–500 jobs, taking Chattanooga capacity above 50,000 tpa; NOVONIX will not close on the land until the conditions precedent to the US$754.8m Department of Energy loan commitment are satisfied, and it had not done so as at the half-year report. The longer-range ambition stated in the going-concern note is at least 150,000 tpa. An option over 17.5 acres adjacent to Riverside, taken on 10 March 2026 at a US$26.5m purchase price and pitched as saving more than US$200m of capital by consolidating the build onto one site, was abandoned on 30 July 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Continuous induction furnace graphitisation — the process technology
productsAndServices.description: The technical basis of the whole company: NOVONIX Generation 3 Continuous Induction Furnace Systems, developed with Harper International Corporation under a December 2020 exclusive-use agreement in which Harper develops and exclusively supplies the thermal-processing systems for the battery anode market and NOVONIX commits to buy from Harper. It replaces the batch Acheson furnace that dominates Chinese graphitisation with a continuous, induction-heated process.
highlights: Continuous rather than batch operation, with claimed increased energy efficiency and no chemical purification step
The company states the process "does not depend on any Chinese equipment, IP, or know-how" — the core of its non-FEOC positioning
Claimed "virtually zero emissions and limited use of chemicals", higher charge rate and longer cycle life, and "highest purity in the market… essentially no contaminants"
Marketed as drop-in: "can be integrated into current cell designs with no material additional costs to cell manufacturers"
Energy input stated as 57% carbon-free, of which 15% renewable; net-zero target 2050

Process flow: petroleum coke → crushing → milling → shaping → [agglomeration] → [calcination] → graphitisation → calcination → [particle coating] → [deagglomeration] → sieving and magnetic separation → packaging
productsAndServices.positioning: The differentiation is as much geopolitical as technical — a graphitisation route that carries no Chinese equipment or licensed technology is what makes the output eligible under sourcing rules that exclude prohibited foreign entities. A material qualification applies to the ownership of that technology. In January 2025 NOVONIX signed a separate exclusive *licence* agreement with Harper for the right to design and develop the furnace technology for its own internal use. It was required to make an initial payment no later than 31 December 2025, did not make it, and the licence agreement automatically expired on 1 January 2026. The December 2020 exclusive supply agreement survives, so the company retains exclusive access — but as a purchaser of Harper's furnaces rather than as a holder of rights to build them, and the 20-F flags the dependency explicitly.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold — an internal process technology, supplied to NOVONIX by Harper International under the 2020 exclusive-use agreement
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Internal use at Riverside and, if built, Enterprise South
productsAndServices.roadmap: No published furnace-technology roadmap beyond the installed Generation 3 systems; the half-year report notes an expected reduction in furnace consumable parts "due to improvements in furnace component technology"

productsAndServices.name: Feedstock and upstream supply
productsAndServices.description: Synthetic graphite is made from petroleum coke, a by-product of oil refining, and NOVONIX's feedstock position runs through its largest shareholder. Phillips 66 invested US$150m for roughly 15% of the company in September 2021, held 90,931,263 shares or about 10.57% at 31 December 2025 after dilution, holds a board seat, and is a key supplier of petroleum coke.
highlights: Technology Development Agreement with Phillips 66 signed January 2022 to identify improved feedstocks
Phillips 66's Lake Charles, Louisiana refinery is identified as a coke source
The Phillips 66 board nominee is Suresh Vaidyanathan, Vice President, Renewable Fuels at Phillips 66
The FY2025 20-F notes that Phillips 66 "has certain rights as a shareholder that are not equal to those of other shareholders"
A domestic petroleum-coke supply is part of the non-Chinese sourcing claim, not merely a commercial convenience
productsAndServices.positioning: A strategic-investor supply relationship rather than an arm's-length one; it gives NOVONIX a US feedstock route but concentrates a critical input and roughly a tenth of the register in the same counterparty
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not applicable — an inbound supply relationship
productsAndServices.roadmap: No dated milestones disclosed for the feedstock programme

productsAndServices.name: Divested and retained interests
productsAndServices.description: Two businesses left the group in eight months, and one small equity interest came back. Battery Technology Solutions — the Nova Scotia battery-testing-equipment and R&D services division founded in 2013 by Dr Chris Burns out of Dr Jeff Dahn's Dalhousie University group and acquired in 2017 — was sold to Burns himself, effective 30 April 2026, for US$1.00, with a US$2m cash balance at close and a trademark licence to 31 December 2026. It now trades as Avrion Battery Labs Inc. and Dryve Battery Materials Inc., and NOVONIX retains a 15% non-dilutable equity stake in Dryve's cathode business.
highlights: BTS made the Ultra-High Precision Coulometry (UHPC) battery-testing systems invented in Jeff Dahn's Dalhousie laboratory, which measure cell cycle life "in weeks instead of years"; a UHPC Calibration Module completed development in November 2025
BTS was the source of all of NOVONIX's reported revenue: US$5.6m in FY2025, US$5.9m in FY2024, US$8.1m in FY2023 — which is why continuing-operations revenue is zero from 2026

The retained 15% stake in Dryve covers an all-dry, zero-waste, precursor-free cathode synthesis platform with foundational patents granted in the US and Europe during 2025 and in China in December 2025, and a pilot line of up to 10 tpa
Dryve's cathode programme carried a Natural Resources Canada award of up to C$5m announced in August 2025

The Mount Dromedary natural graphite project in Northern Queensland was sold to Lithium Energy Limited in September 2025 for A$2m plus repayment of A$250,000, after the planned Axon Graphite IPO was abandoned on 1 August 2025 for market conditions
productsAndServices.positioning: The divestitures are consistent with the company's stated aim of streamlining "around its core synthetic graphite business" and reducing funding requirements — but they also removed every source of revenue the group had
productsAndServices.roadmap: The 15% Dryve interest is a passive holding; no licensing revenue from it is disclosed or guided

recentDevelopments.headline: S&P Dow Jones Indices announces the September 2026 quarterly rebalance of the S&P/ASX indices: NOVONIX (NVX) is listed for removal from the S&P/ASX 300, effective prior to the open of trading on Monday 21 September 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Forced index-fund selling arrives in the same fortnight as the Nasdaq cure deadline and while the ASX price sits below the A$0.12 Yorkville floor — three pressures on the same share price, converging. The removal was read directly from the S&P DJI announcement PDF lodged on the company's investor-relations site; NVX appears in the Removal column of the S&P/ASX 300 section.

recentDevelopments.headline: Half-year report to 30 June 2026 lodged with the ASX: net loss US$24.6m, operating cash outflow US$23.1m, cash US$59.5m, net current liabilities US$2.5m, and a PwC review report flagging a material uncertainty over going concern
recentDevelopments.read: The report also carries the disclosure the market has least priced: the date for Riverside to reach full production capacity moved out by nearly four years, to September 2031. Furnished to the SEC as a Form 6-K on 2 September.

recentDevelopments.headline: The American depositary share ratio changes from one ADS per four ordinary shares to one ADS per forty, taking effect
recentDevelopments.read: Economically a one-for-ten reverse split of the ADSs. Every per-ADS price dated before this day is stale by a factor of ten; ordinary-share prices on the ASX are unaffected because the ordinary share count did not change. Confirmed effective by a Form 424B3 filed 17 August 2026 by the depositary registrant.

recentDevelopments.headline: Change to the American depositary share ratio announced, agreed with The Bank of New York Mellon, expressly to help regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement
recentDevelopments.read: The company disclaims the outcome in the same sentence: "there can be no assurance that the change in the ADS ratio will result in the Company regaining or maintaining compliance". Authorised by Chairman Admiral Robert J. Natter.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2-2026 quarterly activities report: capital expenditure cut to US$2.2m from US$6.8m in Q1, the 17.5-acre Riverside land option abandoned, and the Department of Energy grant confirmed still under review by CMEI
recentDevelopments.read: A 68% quarter-on-quarter capex cut is the clearest measure of the capital-conservation posture that later shows up as the 2031 capacity date.

recentDevelopments.headline: Share purchase plan closes having raised A$962,600 from 6,016,250 shares at A$0.16
recentDevelopments.read: Against a placement of A$20.7m at the same price days earlier, retail take-up of under A$1m is a weak signal on existing-shareholder appetite. The close had been brought forward from 14 August to 17 July.

recentDevelopments.headline: ASX grants waivers of Listing Rules 7.1 and 10.11 for the June placement
recentDevelopments.read: The waivers were needed because the A$0.16 offer price was below 80% of the five-day volume-weighted average price — a mechanical disclosure that quantifies how deep the discount was.

recentDevelopments.headline: Ron Edmonds takes the interim Chief Financial Officer role and steps aside as Chair; Admiral Robert J. Natter resumes as Chairman
recentDevelopments.read: A director serving as interim CFO while the company carries a going-concern material uncertainty is a governance point a counterparty would weigh. Edmonds was Chief Accounting Officer of Dow; he remains a director. The company's own leadership page still shows Natter as Deputy Chairman and is stale on this point.

recentDevelopments.headline: Institutional placement completed: 129,334,163 shares at A$0.16 raising A$20.7m, about US$14.5m, through Bell Potter
recentDevelopments.read: The raise price is 73% below the A$0.60 Phillips 66 placement of January 2025 and a third below the pre-halt trade. Dilution is the recurring cost of a pre-revenue build.

recentDevelopments.headline: First known North-American-produced synthetic graphite anode active material C-sample delivered to Panasonic Energy; internal testing indicates it meets Panasonic's specifications
recentDevelopments.read: The single most important technical milestone the company has reached, and the gate the going-concern assessment turns on. A C-sample is 5–30 tonnes produced on production equipment, with customer feedback typically taking 6–12 months — which lands the answer in roughly mid-2027 against a second-half-2027 start of production, leaving essentially no slack.

recentDevelopments.headline: Chief Financial Officer Robert Long to depart in July; board leadership rearranged in consequence
recentDevelopments.read: Long had been CFO since September 2024 and interim chief executive from January to May 2025.

recentDevelopments.headline: United States Senator Marsha Blackburn tours the Riverside facility
recentDevelopments.read: Political support is a real asset for a company whose economics depend on federal grants, credits and a loan commitment — and whose trade case has just failed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sale of NOVONIX Battery Technology Solutions Inc. to former chief executive Dr Chris Burns completes, effective 30 April 2026, for US$1.00 plus a retained 15% stake in the cathode business
recentDevelopments.read: The transaction that made NOVONIX a single-business, zero-revenue company. BTS now operates as Avrion Battery Labs and Dryve Battery Materials; the US$1.00 price is the clearest available statement of what the divested business was worth on a standalone basis after funding requirements.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1-2026 quarterly activities report records that the International Trade Commission's March decision means the proposed antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese anode material will not be implemented
recentDevelopments.read: In the company's own words: "As a result, previously proposed antidumping and countervailing duties will not be implemented." The annual general meeting on 15 April passed all resolutions and Nick Liveris retired from the board.

recentDevelopments.headline: The United States government certifies the Riverside project in connection with the US$103m Section 48C investment tax credit, certification dated 8 April 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The credit is payable when the first 11,000 tpa is placed in service, provided that happens before 7 April 2028 — a deadline that sits awkwardly beside a September 2031 full-capacity date. The credits are transferable and can be sold to a third party, which makes them a financing instrument as well as a tax asset.

recentDevelopments.headline: Nasdaq Listing Qualifications notifies NOVONIX that the closing bid price of its ADSs has been below US$1.00 for 30 consecutive business days; 180 calendar days to regain compliance
recentDevelopments.read: The cure test is a closing bid of at least US$1.00 for ten consecutive business days within the period. 180 days from 18 March 2026 is Monday 14 September 2026. Authorised by Chairman Ron Edmonds.

recentDevelopments.headline: The US International Trade Commission votes 2-1 that imports of active anode material from China do not materially retard the establishment of a United States industry — so no antidumping or countervailing duty orders are issued
recentDevelopments.read: The most consequential event of the period, and it went against the company. NOVONIX was a named petitioner through the American Active Anode Material Producers coalition. Commerce had set final duties in February at 93.5% antidumping (102.72% China-wide) and 66.82–66.86% countervailing, all conditional on an affirmative injury finding that never came. The financial consequence is quantified in NOVONIX's own June impairment model, which cut the assumed selling price from US$10–12/kg to US$7–11/kg and named the Commerce ruling as the reason.

recentDevelopments.headline: Exclusive access agreement with Aerisyn Opportunity Zone Business, LLC to assess purchase of 17.5 acres adjacent to Riverside at US$26.5m
recentDevelopments.read: Pitched as saving more than US$200m of capital by consolidating the 50,000 tpa build onto one site. Abandoned four and a half months later.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025 Form 20-F filed: revenue US$5.6m, net loss US$92.7m, cash US$79.9m; PwC's audit report carries a going-concern explanatory paragraph and management reports material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting
recentDevelopments.read: Two separate red flags in one document. The audit opinion itself is unqualified, but disclosure controls were reported not effective at 31 December 2025 and a segregation-of-duties material weakness remained unremediated.

recentDevelopments.headline: Binding term sheet to divest Battery Technology Solutions to former chief executive Dr Chris Burns for US$1.00
recentDevelopments.read: Framed as a portfolio decision — "to focus on synthetic graphite" — and reducing ongoing funding requirements.

recentDevelopments.headline: Commerce issues final antidumping and countervailing determinations on Chinese active anode material: 93.5% antidumping for specified companies, 102.72% China-wide, 66.82–66.86% countervailing, a stacked total above 160%
recentDevelopments.read: NOVONIX publicised this as vindication. It was conditional on the ITC injury finding that failed four weeks later, so none of it took effect — a case study in why a Commerce determination is not a duty.

recentDevelopments.headline: Panasonic mass production pushed from 2026 to the second half of 2027
recentDevelopments.read: An eighteen-month slip in the start of revenue, and past the Q4-2025 qualification milestone that conditioned the Panasonic offtake's volume commitment.

recentDevelopments.headline: The January 2025 exclusive licence agreement with Harper International for the continuous induction furnace technology expires automatically, the required initial payment not having been made by 31 December 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The company forgoes the right to design and develop its own furnaces and remains dependent on Harper to manufacture and supply them under the separate 2020 agreement. A capital-conservation decision with a long tail, and one that no press release announced.

recentDevelopments.headline: Michael O'Kronley appointed Managing Director, joining the board
recentDevelopments.read: Consolidates the chief executive he had been since May 2025 with a board seat.

recentDevelopments.headline: Stellantis terminates its offtake agreement with immediate effect, the parties "unable to agree upon the unique battery cell product specifications and milestones for mass production qualification"
recentDevelopments.read: The largest contracted volume NOVONIX ever held — a minimum 86,250 tonnes and a target of 115,000 tonnes over six years, signed November 2024 with supply targeted from January 2026 — is gone. It is also the clearest precedent for how a qualification failure ends.

recentDevelopments.headline: First mass-production, commercial-grade sample of synthetic graphite shipped for industrial applications
recentDevelopments.read: Proves the furnace line at production scale, though for a lower-value non-battery product and to an unnamed customer with no supply agreement announced.

recentDevelopments.headline: Funding agreement with YA II PN, Ltd, an affiliate of Yorkville Advisors Global, for up to US$100m face of unsecured convertible debentures issued at 95% of face
recentDevelopments.read: Introduces the A$0.12 floor price and the Amortization Event that now dominates the balance-sheet risk. Fully drawn within three months. Goldman Sachs was exclusive financial adviser.

recentDevelopments.headline: Founder Dr Chris Burns steps down as chief executive
recentDevelopments.read: He remained a special adviser to the board until January 2026 and became the buyer of Battery Technology Solutions in April 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Department of Energy conditional commitment of up to US$754.8m for the second facility
recentDevelopments.read: US$692.0m of principal plus US$62.8m of capitalised interest. Still conditional in every filing through 31 August 2026, and the reason the Enterprise South land purchase has not closed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Binding offtake agreement with PowerCo SE, Volkswagen's cell company: a minimum 32,000 tonnes over five years from 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Conditioned on qualification milestones, compliance criteria and — the condition that matters now — NOVONIX "securing financing commitments for the production facilities", failing which PowerCo may terminate.

recentDevelopments.headline: Binding offtake agreement with Panasonic Energy for at least 10,000 tonnes of anode material for its US plants
recentDevelopments.read: The volume commitment was conditioned on NOVONIX meeting mass-production qualification milestones before the fourth quarter of 2025. That milestone was not met; Panasonic may reduce the volume by up to 20% or terminate if the delay is substantial, and no public exercise of either right has been announced.

relationships.note: Panasonic Energy is NOVONIX's lead customer under a binding offtake for at least 10,000 tonnes of anode active material for its US plants; the half-year report names it as "our lead customer".
relationships.context:
The offtake was signed on 8 February 2024 for at least 10,000 tonnes of synthetic graphite anode active material for Panasonic Energy's United States plants. The volume commitment was conditioned on NOVONIX achieving mass-production qualification milestones before the fourth quarter of 2025; if missed, Panasonic may reduce the volume by up to 20%, or terminate if the delay is substantial.

That milestone was not met. Panasonic mass production was pushed from 2026 to the second half of 2027 on 16 January 2026 and reaffirmed at that date since. NOVONIX delivered a C-sample on 11 June 2026 — the first known synthetic graphite AAM C-sample produced in North America — and states that its own internal testing indicates the material meets Panasonic's specifications, with formal validation by Panasonic still outstanding as at 31 August 2026. No public exercise of Panasonic's reduction or termination rights has been announced.

The dependency runs deeper than a supply contract. The first of the four conditions the directors list in their going-concern assessment is "the Company achieving qualification status (being able to mass produce qualifying products for Panasonic and other future offtake customers and achieve the respective customer's quality standards)". Panasonic's validation decision is therefore a solvency input, not merely a commercial one.

relationships.note: LG Energy Solution holds US$30m of NOVONIX convertible loan notes and is described by NOVONIX as a joint-development-agreement counterparty — not as an offtake customer.
relationships.context:
On 21 June 2023 LG Energy Solution subscribed for 45,221,586 convertible loan notes of A$1.00 face, carrying a 4% coupon and maturing 7 June 2028, for proceeds of US$30 million, with a conversion price of A$1.60. The FY2025 20-F describes the commercial side of the relationship as a "joint development agreement with LGES", not an offtake.

The instrument's own terms make a point the prose does not. The notes **mandatorily convert upon acceptance of the first purchase order under the purchase agreement with LGES** — and they remained outstanding at 30 June 2026. It follows from the notes' continued existence that no purchase order has ever been accepted. This is an inference from the conversion trigger and the balance-sheet position, both first-party disclosures, rather than a statement either party has made.

The notes are classified as current because the company cannot defer settlement, so they sit alongside the Yorkville debentures in the near-term liability stack rather than as patient strategic capital.

relationships.note: Not a commercial relationship — a shared policy exposure. AES Clean Energy's dossier records the antidumping and countervailing investigations into Chinese graphite as pending; NOVONIX was a petitioner in those cases and its filings carry the outcome.
relationships.context:
AES Clean Energy's dossier states that the AD/CVD investigations into Chinese natural and synthetic graphite for lithium-ion anode material had "final determinations expected in the first quarter of 2026" and could result in price increases. NOVONIX's own filings close that question from the petitioner's side.

Commerce issued final determinations on 13 February 2026 — 93.5% antidumping for specified companies, 102.72% China-wide, and 66.82–66.86% countervailing. On 12 March 2026 the International Trade Commission voted 2-1 that the imports do not materially retard the establishment of a United States industry, so **no antidumping or countervailing duty order was issued and none of those rates took effect**. NOVONIX records the result plainly: "previously proposed antidumping and countervailing duties will not be implemented."

The two companies sit on opposite sides of the same measure — a battery buyer that would have paid the duty, and a domestic producer that petitioned for it. Recording the link makes the corpus's answer to the open question findable from either end.

policyExposure.regime: AD/CVD — active anode material from China
policyExposure.exposure: NOVONIX was a named petitioner, through the American Active Anode Material Producers coalition, in the antidumping and countervailing duty cases against Chinese active anode material, filed December 2024. Commerce set final rates on 13 February 2026 — antidumping 93.5% for specified companies and 102.72% China-wide, countervailing 66.82–66.86%, a stacked total the company publicised as above 160%. All of it was conditional on an affirmative injury determination. On 12 March 2026 the International Trade Commission voted 2-1 that the imports do not materially retard the establishment of a United States industry, so no duty order issued and none of the rates took effect. The company states it plainly: "previously proposed antidumping and countervailing duties will not be implemented", and elsewhere "ultimately unsuccessful following a split decision (2-1) by the ITC on the question of material retardation". The financial consequence is quantified in NOVONIX's own June 2026 impairment model, which cut the assumed realised price from US$10–12/kg to US$7–11/kg and names the Commerce ruling as the reason.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company notes that the two commissioners who voted against have since been replaced and that with a full complement of six only three affirmative votes are needed, and states that it "intends to consider filing a new AD/CVD petition at an appropriate time", subject to market conditions and the factual record.

policyExposure.exposure: Three layers, and the company's own two published totals differ because they describe different dates. A 25% Section 301 tariff on battery-grade graphite from China was reinstated in June 2024. The US Trade Representative then completed a forced-labour investigation and imposed 10%–12.5% tariffs on most goods including synthetic graphite from 59 countries and the European Union. A second Section 301 investigation, into structural excess manufacturing capacity across 16 countries and the EU, remains open; NOVONIX has submitted comments and testified in support. A Section 122 tariff of 10% was in place until the second half of July 2026. The two figures the company publishes are 35% and 37.5% — the Q1-2026 quarterly report and the half-year highlights say "existing tariffs of 35% remain in place", while the half-year impairment note assumes "current tariffs (37.5%)". Both appear in first-party documents; the difference is the date each describes, and neither is corrected here.
policyExposure.mitigation: NOVONIX positions itself as the domestic alternative and lobbies for measures that "address this structural price imbalance", including product-specific tariff classifications for graphite anode material.

policyExposure.exposure: A US$103m investment tax credit allocated in April 2024 under the Qualifying Advanced Energy Project Allocation Program, with the Riverside project certified by the United States government on 8 April 2026. Nothing has been claimed. The credit vests only when the first 11,000 tonnes per annum is placed in service, and only if that happens before 7 April 2028. Against a full-capacity date of September 2031 and a second-half-2027 start of mass production, the 2028 condition is the binding constraint on a US$103m asset.
policyExposure.mitigation: The credits are transferable and can be sold to a third party, which makes them a financing instrument rather than only a tax asset — but only once earned.

policyExposure.exposure: Graphite, including synthetic graphite, remains eligible for the 45X credit, worth 10% of eligible production costs for critical minerals; the Enterprise South site is described as eligible for a potential 45X credit. The credit for battery cells is US$35 per kilowatt-hour, and eligibility depends on increasing limits on material assistance from prohibited foreign entities, measured as the proportion of direct material and production costs from non-prohibited sources: 65% for cells sold in 2027, rising to a maximum of 85% in 2030 and thereafter. Under current law the credit is reduced 25% in 2030, 50% in 2031 and 75% in 2032 before expiring for cells after 2032. NOVONIX's commercial argument to customers is that non-Chinese anode material is what lets *their* cells qualify.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company is lobbying Treasury for revisions to the material cost ratio tables and methodologies, clarification of the "prohibited foreign entity" definition and related ownership and control concepts, and anti-circumvention measures.

policyExposure.exposure: Phased sourcing requirements for advanced batteries procured by the United States Department of Defense. From 2028, for new acquisition programs, the Department generally may procure only advanced batteries and cells whose functional cell components and technology are not owned, sourced, refined or produced by a foreign entity of concern, with a limited exception where final assembly occurs outside an FEOC, more than 95% of the cost of functional cell components is attributable to non-FEOC sources, and the battery is produced without FEOC-licensed technology. The requirements expand to standard batteries in 2029 and to existing acquisition programs in 2031. This is the regime NOVONIX's claim that its process "does not depend on any Chinese equipment, IP, or know-how" is written against.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company states that it and the industry "have been working closely with Department of Defense personnel on implementing regulations to ensure that the interests of the U.S. domestic graphite AAM industry are properly addressed". Note a naming inconsistency across two first-party documents four weeks apart: the half-year report calls the procuring agency the Department of War, the Q2 quarterly report the Department of Defense.

policyExposure.exposure: Commerce concluded that imports of processed critical minerals and their derivatives threaten to impair national security; the President concurred and on 14 January 2026 issued a proclamation directing Commerce and the Trade Representative to negotiate agreements with trading partners, specifically contemplating price floors for trade in processed critical minerals. A price floor would be a more direct remedy for NOVONIX's economics than a tariff, because the problem it describes is a price set by subsidised competitors rather than a volume of imports.
policyExposure.mitigation: A 180-day status report to the President was due on 13 July 2026 and, in the company's words, "no public announcement has been made regarding that report". If satisfactory agreements are not reached, the administration may impose tariffs, minimum import prices or other remedies.

policyExposure.regime: Chinese export controls on graphite and graphitisation equipment
policyExposure.exposure: China imposed export controls on certain graphite items from 1 December 2023, tightened them in December 2024, and again in October 2025 — the October round covering synthetic and blended graphite anode material and the equipment, processes and technology used to make it, including graphitisation furnaces, granulation machines and coating equipment. For a Western entrant this cuts both ways: it restricts the competing supply and it restricts the equipment route most entrants would otherwise use.
policyExposure.mitigation: NOVONIX's furnace technology is supplied by Harper International in the United States and the company states it depends on no Chinese equipment, intellectual property or know-how. Per the company's November 2025 investor presentation the October 2025 controls have since been suspended until November 2026.

policyExposure.regime: Critical minerals designation — US Geological Survey
policyExposure.exposure: Synthetic graphite is on the United States Geological Survey critical minerals list, which is the predicate for the Department of Energy grant, the Section 48C allocation, the Department of Energy loan commitment and the Section 232 proceeding. The company's framing is that designation alone is insufficient: "U.S. producers must still compete with imported materials whose prices may be influenced by significant foreign government support and other non-market factors."

policyExposure.regime: Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) — minimum bid price
policyExposure.exposure: On 18 March 2026 Nasdaq's Listing Qualifications Department notified NOVONIX that the closing bid price of its American depositary shares had been below US$1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, opening a 180-calendar-day compliance period that ends on Monday 14 September 2026. To cure, the closing bid must be at least US$1.00 for a minimum of ten consecutive business days within the period. The ASX listing of the ordinary shares is unaffected. The outcome is unresolved as at 9 September 2026, and it is unresolved for an arithmetic reason as well as an evidentiary one: the ADS ratio change that raised the price took effect on 27 August 2026, and counting business days from that date — with the United States market closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day — the tenth consecutive qualifying session cannot fall before Thursday 10 September 2026, one day after this dossier was written. Eight qualifying closes had completed, from 27 August to 8 September inclusive. No announcement of regained compliance exists on EDGAR, whose most recent NOVONIX filing of any kind is the 2 September 6-K, or on the company's ASX announcements list, whose most recent item is dated 4 September.
policyExposure.mitigation: The ADS ratio change from 1:4 to 1:40, effective 27 August 2026 — economically a one-for-ten reverse split of the ADSs — was made expressly to raise the per-ADS price, with the company disclaiming any assurance that it would work.

financials.commentary:
Reported in US dollars under IFRS as issued by the IASB, by an Australian company dual-listed on the ASX and Nasdaq. Two presentation breaks matter. First, the Battery Technology Solutions divestiture on 30 April 2026 moved that division to discontinued operations under AASB 5, and comparatives were re-presented — so continuing-operations revenue is zero in both halves shown, and the US$5–8m revenue lines in the annual columns are the divested equipment business, not the graphite business. Second, the ADS ratio changed from 1:4 to 1:40 on 27 August 2026, so per-ADS figures are not comparable across that date; per-share figures below are per ordinary share and are unaffected.

Collection gap on expectations. There is no usable published analyst consensus for FY2024, FY2025 or H1-2026. The one aggregator carrying broker entries shows two, both stale by more than eighteen months and both stated on the old 1:4 ADS — a Jefferies Buy at US$2.60 from November 2024 and a Chardan Buy at US$4.00 from May 2024, which on the current ratio would be US$26.00 and US$40.00. Any current "consensus target" that mixes those with a post-27-August ADS price is arithmetically corrupt. Every `expected` field below is therefore left empty rather than reconstructed.

strategyRead: **KEY JUDGMENTS** — analysis by the author, not sourced fact. Confidence bands follow the intelligence-community convention: high, moderate, low.

1. **(High confidence)** We assess that NOVONIX is best typed as a pre-commercial aspirant rather than an incumbent or a challenger in anode materials, and that the gap is one of scale rather than of technology. Basis: continuing-operations revenue is zero and has never been otherwise; the Riverside nameplate of 20,000 tpa is under 1% of the 2.11 million tonnes of global anode shipments SNE Research counted for 2024, and about 4.6% of BTR's single-company volume; all ten of the largest producers are Chinese, with POSCO Future M having fallen to eleventh. The company's own claim — "the only qualified U.S.-based supplier of battery-grade synthetic graphite anode material" — is a claim about a national market with almost no production in it, and it is compatible with holding no share of the global one.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the September 2031 full-capacity date is the most important disclosure in the half-year report, and that it has not been absorbed by the surrounding commentary. Basis: the revised ramp-up timeline "extends the expected date to achieve full production capacity from December 2027 to September 2031", stated in Note 6 as a conscious decision to conserve capital. A near-four-year slip changes the character of every dated obligation around it: the Section 48C credit requires 11,000 tpa in service before 7 April 2028, the PowerCo offtake runs 2027 to 2031, and the Panasonic offtake's original window was 2025 to 2028. A capital-conservation decision taken to protect solvency has moved the plant past the deadlines that make the plant worth financing.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that the Yorkville floor price converts a share-price problem into a cash-solvency problem, and that this is the mechanism most likely to determine the company's near-term outcome. Basis: an Amortization Event occurs where the daily volume-weighted average price on the ASX is below the A$0.12 floor on any five of any seven consecutive trading days, and on occurrence NOVONIX "may be required to redeem in cash 20%" of the US$35.0m outstanding — about US$7.0m — with the requirement recurring at 30-day intervals while the circumstances continue. The ordinary shares closed at about A$0.098 on 9 September 2026, roughly 18% below the floor. Against a cash balance of US$59.5m consuming about US$23m a half, a recurring 20% redemption is material rather than nominal, and the directors list "funding any cash redemption requirements that may arise under the Yorkville funding agreement" as one of the four conditions on which going concern depends.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the failure of the trade case is the most under-reported event in this company's year, and that it did more damage than the Nasdaq notice it preceded by six days. Basis: Commerce set final duties above 160% in February 2026 and the company publicised them; on 12 March 2026 the International Trade Commission voted 2-1 that the imports do not materially retard the establishment of a US industry, so no order issued and none of the rates took effect. NOVONIX itself priced the consequence four months later, cutting the assumed realised price in its impairment model from US$10–12/kg to US$7–11/kg and naming the Commerce ruling as the reason. A roughly 20–30% cut to the assumed selling price of the only product the company makes is a larger event than a listing-compliance notice, and it received a fraction of the attention.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the qualification record, not the technology, is the binding constraint — and that there is a precedent for how qualification failure ends. Basis: Stellantis terminated its offtake on 4 November 2025 because the parties were "unable to agree upon the unique battery cell product specifications and milestones for mass production qualification", removing a minimum 86,250 tonnes and a target of 115,000. The Panasonic milestone that conditioned its volume commitment was missed. The LG Energy Solution notes mandatorily convert on acceptance of the first purchase order under the purchase agreement and remain outstanding, from which it follows that no purchase order has ever been accepted. Three counterparty relationships, three qualification gates, and not one crossed. The C-sample delivered in June 2026 is genuine progress against that record, but the feedback window on a C-sample is typically six to twelve months, which lands the answer around mid-2027 against a second-half-2027 production start.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that this is a policy-created business whose policy support is real but conditional at every point, and that the conditionality is systematically understated in summaries of it. Basis: of the roughly US$958m of headline government support, only about US$48.7m has actually been received. The US$100m Department of Energy grant has US$51.3m still to claim and is disclosed in two consecutive quarterly reports as **under review** by the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, with no first-party statement that the review has concluded. The US$103m Section 48C credit is certified but unclaimed and vests only on 11,000 tpa in service before April 2028. The US$754.8m Department of Energy loan is a conditional commitment whose conditions precedent have not been satisfied — which is why the Enterprise South land has not been bought. A useful comparison is that a peer petitioner, Anovion, had its Department of Energy grant cancelled in October 2025 while NOVONIX's survived.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the lapse of the Harper licence signals capital rationing reaching into strategic assets rather than a change of technical direction. Basis: the January 2025 exclusive licence to design and develop the continuous induction furnace technology for internal use expired automatically on 1 January 2026 because NOVONIX did not make the required initial payment by 31 December 2025. The December 2020 exclusive use and supply agreement survives, so exclusivity is retained; what was given up is the option to build furnaces independently of Harper. Confidence is low because no company statement explains the decision and the omission of a payment could equally reflect a renegotiation, a change of plan, or a judgement that the supply agreement suffices.

8. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that NOVONIX's exposure to grid-scale storage is real at the level of the chemistry and absent at the level of the contracts, and that a storage-focused reader should hold both facts at once. Basis: graphite anodes are chemistry-agnostic, so the LFP cells that make up roughly 90% of battery storage use them as surely as vehicle cells do, and third-party estimates put energy storage at about 18% of anode-material demand in 2026 against about 69% for vehicles. NOVONIX names energy storage among its target segments and cites storage-installation growth as a demand driver. But **both binding offtakes are with electric-vehicle cell makers** — Panasonic Energy for US vehicle plants and PowerCo for Volkswagen — and no storage-specific agreement is disclosed. The exposure is to total lithium-ion demand, of which storage is the fastest-growing minority.

**Collection gaps.** Whether Nasdaq compliance has been regained is unresolved and, as at 9 September 2026, arithmetically incapable of resolution — see the policy exposure entry for the day count. No NOVONIX securities class action or short-seller report was identified; the correct record is "none identified". No analyst consensus exists for any period covered. The outcome of the Department of Energy grant review is not stated in any filing. The status of Dwayne Johnson, appointed Chief Operating Officer on 3 November 2025, cannot be established: he is absent from the current leadership page and from the half-year report, with no departure announcement located, so the record here is "no longer listed" rather than "departed". NOVONIX's own FY2025 20-F gives two different registered-office addresses — Level 38, 71 Eagle Street in Item 4.A and a care-of address at Level 11, Central Plaza Two, 66 Eagle Street in the corporate directory — and which it regards as authoritative could not be determined. No contract pricing is public for either offtake.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH.** *Thursday 10 September 2026 — the tenth qualifying session:* the earliest date on which the ten-consecutive-business-day test can complete, counting from the 27 August ratio change and excluding Labor Day. *Monday 14 September 2026 — the Nasdaq cure deadline:* compliance regained, an extension granted, or a delisting determination; there is no fourth outcome, and the margin between the earliest possible cure and the deadline is two business days. *Monday 21 September 2026 — removal from the S&P/ASX 300 takes effect:* forced index selling into a price already below the Yorkville floor. *Any Amortization Event notice:* five sub-floor closes in seven trading days triggers it, and the ASX price has been below A$0.12 since before this dossier was written. *Panasonic's formal validation of the June C-sample:* the single event that would convert the qualification record from three failures to one success, expected on a six-to-twelve-month feedback cycle. *The Department of Energy grant review:* any statement that it has concluded, in either direction, moves US$51.3m. *7 April 2028 — the Section 48C in-service deadline:* against a September 2031 full-capacity date, the first 11,000 tpa either lands in time or a certified US$103m credit lapses.
